source: Revision 2 (docs/framework-research/09-hiring-workflows-draft.md §1, approved by the owner 2026-11-08), rewritten as revision 3 on 2026-11-09 from the owner's comments after his own run of the on-site pilot (docs/framework-research/15-pilot-on-site.md §14): one stage at a time, every step in plain language, a three-way answer per step, open questions at decision points, the chart as a whole at the stage level. Company perspective only; the candidate perspective is not shown to employer-side participants. The step ids are unchanged from revision 2. Amended 2026-11-10 after the owner's review of revision 3: a notes box on every step whatever the answer, each stage's entry and exit named on its diagram, and the stage questions say to leave the box empty if there is nothing.
intro: This is our picture of how a hire runs, from the first sign that a role is needed to the lessons kept when the search closes. It is not how your organisation does it. You are asked to say, stage by stage and step by step, where it matches and where it does not.
overview_question: Does a hire where you work pass through these five stages, in this order? If not, what is different?
differs_prompt: How does it run where you work, and who does it?
decision_question: What can happen at this point where you work? List the outcomes.

phase_questions.text: Where you work, are two of the steps above really one step? Which two? Leave the box empty if not.
Who writes the role's requirements where you work, and who signs them off? Leave the box empty if not.

missing_question: Is there a step in this stage that happens where you work and is not here? One per box; leave it empty if not.

closing.text: Is there anything on this chart you would not want a candidate to see?
Where in this picture does a hire get put on hold where you work, and what brings it back?

phases.title: Need and approval
phases.purpose: Someone decides a role is needed, and someone who owns a budget agrees to it.
phases.leaves_with: an approved request, or a denial or a deferral

phases.title: Role definition
phases.purpose: The hiring manager writes down what the role is and what it takes to do it, and HR checks that the definition is complete and within policy.

phases.title: Sourcing and screening
phases.purpose: Candidates come in and are narrowed to a short list the hiring manager will meet.
phases.leaves_with: a short list the hiring manager has accepted

phases.title: Assessment and decision
phases.purpose: The hiring manager meets the candidates, chooses one, and an offer is made.
phases.enters_with: a short list the hiring manager has accepted

phases.title: Onboarding and outcome
phases.purpose: The person starts, and the company learns whether the hire worked.
phases.leaves_with: a closed search and the record of the hire

nodes.name: A role is needed
nodes.owner: The hiring manager
nodes.summary: Someone leaves, the work grows, or new work arrives. At this point there is usually nothing written down.

nodes.name: A request for the role is written
nodes.owner: The hiring manager
nodes.summary: The manager writes up why the role is needed, at what level, what it will cost, when it is needed, and whether it replaces someone or adds a person.

nodes.name: The request is reviewed
nodes.owner: Finance, HR, the manager's own manager, the head of the department
nodes.summary: They check the budget and the headcount plan, and whether the work could be covered another way: spread across the team, a contractor, or automation.

nodes.name: The request is approved, or not
nodes.owner: Whoever owns the budget, on the reviewers' advice
nodes.summary: The request is approved, turned down with a reason, or put off until a later date. In our picture a request put off past its date without a review is escalated.
nodes.decision_question: What can happen to a request at this point where you work? List the outcomes.
our_outcomes: Put off until a later date
Put off past its date without a review, and escalated

nodes.name: HR keeps a standard form for defining a role
nodes.owner: HR
nodes.summary: A standing template that says what a role definition must contain: the purpose of the role, its requirements and how much each matters, the level and the pay range. HR owns the form and changes it rarely.

nodes.name: The manager writes the role definition and its requirements
nodes.owner: The hiring manager, who is responsible for the content
nodes.summary: Using the form, the manager writes what the role is for, what it must deliver, each requirement with how much it matters and what would count as equivalent, the level, the pay range, the location and the working conditions.

nodes.name: HR checks the definition
nodes.owner: HR, with legal where needed
nodes.summary: HR checks that the definition is complete and within policy and pay rules. It passes, goes back to the manager with a list of what to fix, or is held until a later date. HR does not second-guess the requirements themselves.
our_outcomes: Goes back to the manager with a list of what to fix
nodes.returns_when: when the definition does not pass

nodes.name: The job posting is written and published
nodes.owner: The recruiter writes it; the hiring manager approves the text
nodes.summary: The posting is written from the role definition. In our picture the definition is the source and the posting is a copy of it, never the other way round.

nodes.name: Applications come in
nodes.owner: The recruiter
nodes.summary: People apply, are referred, or are approached directly. Together they are the pool.

nodes.name: Hard rules remove some applicants
nodes.owner: The recruiter, through rules set in the applicant tracking system
nodes.summary: Applicants who cannot be hired are removed: no right to work, wrong location, a licence missing. Today keyword rules often sit here too, and they are the first place a qualified person is lost.

nodes.name: Each remaining candidate is screened against the requirements
nodes.owner: The recruiter or an HR screener
nodes.summary: The screener compares each requirement in the posting against what the candidate's documents actually show, one requirement at a time, and asks the candidate about anything that is unclear before deciding. The match record you read belongs to this step.

nodes.name: The screen decision
nodes.owner: The recruiter; the hiring manager can check or overrule any judgement
nodes.summary: Each candidate goes forward, is turned down, is held until a later date, or is sent to the hiring manager because a judgement needs the manager's knowledge.
our_outcomes: Sent to the hiring manager for a judgement that needs the manager's knowledge

nodes.name: The recruiter calls the candidate
nodes.owner: The recruiter
nodes.summary: Interest, timing, pay expectations, practical constraints. Anything still unclear from the screen is asked here and the answers are written down.

nodes.name: The short list goes to the hiring manager
nodes.owner: The recruiter hands it over; the hiring manager decides
nodes.summary: The manager accepts the list, removes individual people from it, or sends the whole list back, either for more candidates or because the role definition needs to change. We do not know whether managers remove individuals before interviewing often enough for this to count as a decision step; you can tell us.
nodes.decision_question: What can happen to a short list at this point where you work? List the outcomes, and say whether the hiring manager removes individual people before interviewing.
our_outcomes: Sends the list back for more candidates
Sends the list back because the role definition needs to change

nodes.name: Interviews
nodes.owner: The hiring manager and the other interviewers; the recruiter organises
nodes.summary: The manager and the interviewers meet the candidates and judge what documents cannot show: how the person works and communicates. In our picture, interviews spend their time first on the requirements the screen could not settle.

nodes.name: A test or a work sample, where used
nodes.owner: The hiring manager or the interviewers
nodes.summary: Some roles ask the candidate to do a piece of work or a test. Not every hire has this step.

nodes.name: The hire decision
nodes.owner: The hiring manager, with the interviewers' views and HR's advice
nodes.summary: One candidate is chosen; or no one is chosen and the search goes on with new candidates; or no one is chosen and the role definition is changed first; or the decision is put off to a later date. In our picture the decision is written down next to the screening record, so the outcome can be traced back to it.
our_outcomes: No one is chosen; the search goes on with new candidates
No one is chosen; the role definition is changed first
The decision is put off to a later date

nodes.name: The offer is put together
nodes.owner: HR and compensation, with the hiring manager
nodes.summary: HR and compensation put the offer together with the hiring manager. If the pay is outside the approved range, it goes back to whoever owns the budget.

nodes.name: The candidate answers the offer
nodes.owner: The candidate decides; the recruiter handles it
nodes.summary: The candidate accepts, negotiates, declines, or does not answer. In our picture no answer by an agreed date counts as declined and is raised with the head of recruiting.
nodes.decision_question: What can happen once an offer is out, where you work? List the outcomes.
our_outcomes: No answer by the agreed date, treated as declined

nodes.name: The other candidates are told
nodes.owner: The recruiter
nodes.summary: Candidates who were not chosen are told, with a real reason where policy allows one. A screen that was written down requirement by requirement makes a real reason easy to give.

nodes.name: Checks and paperwork before the start date
nodes.owner: HR
nodes.summary: Background checks, references, documents, equipment. If a check fails, the decision goes back to the hiring manager or the offer is withdrawn.

nodes.name: The person starts
nodes.owner: The hiring manager and HR
nodes.summary: First days and onboarding. The person is in the role.

nodes.name: A check-in at about 30 days
nodes.owner: The hiring manager and the new employee
nodes.summary: How is it going, from both sides.

nodes.name: A review at about 90 days
nodes.owner: The hiring manager, the employee and HR
nodes.summary: Is the person right for the role and doing it well: confirmed, probation extended, or the person leaves.

nodes.name: How the hire is doing at six to twelve months
nodes.owner: The hiring manager; the HR system
nodes.summary: Whether the person stayed and how they are performing. In our picture this is the information that shows whether the screening got it right.

nodes.name: The search is closed and the lessons are kept
nodes.owner: The recruiter and the hiring manager
nodes.summary: The search is closed. What took how long, which judgements were overruled, and which holds happened are kept as the record of the hire.
